newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FAA chief Hinson announces his resignation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FAA chief Hinson announces his resignation.

text.p: Federal Aviation Administrator David Hinson will resign, as planned, at the end of this week, the agency announced on Thursday.
A successor has not been announced.
Hinson, 63, had said that when he took office in 1993 that he would leave after the 1996 presidential election.

The FAA said that Deputy Administrator Linda Daschle would become acting administrator until shortly after the first of the year. She is the wife of Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle, Democrat of South Dakota.
Hinson has said he counts among his accomplishments an internal reform of the agency, including speeding up modernization of the nation's ageing air traffic control system.

During his tenure, Congress passed legislation that allowed the FAA to write its own personnel and procurement rules so it could respond more quickly to the nation's increased air traffic and to buy the new technology to cope with it.
Before taking over the agency, a part of the Transportation Department, he had been a commercial airline pilot and airline executive.
